headline: The United Arab Emirates has made AI a required school subject from kindergarten to grade 12, teaching young children how it works and fails rather than letting them use it freely.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a national first in education with a clear contrast to the restrictions elsewhere, but the article gives no results yet and no date for the mandate.
importance_line: Schoolchildren and parents in the UAE are affected first, then 22,000 teachers due for training and governments choosing between teaching and restricting AI, but the article reports no learning results and says the UAE's small, well-funded system is hard for larger countries to copy.
summary: Rest of World reports that the United Arab Emirates recently became the first country to make AI a required subject from kindergarten to grade 12, with schools teaching young children through discussion, stories and role-play how AI works and where it fails, and the government planning to train 22,000 teachers to use it. The outlet sets this against New York City's one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI up to grade eight and Norway's near-ban in primary school, and quotes Edward Tsoi, chief executive of the nonprofit AI Safety Asia, warning against handing children AI tools before they have built their own reasoning skills.
notes: Full text read. The article says the mandate came 'recently' and gives no date, so it is treated as new coverage. Abu Dhabi's education department did not respond.
